questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The nature, the academic level and reputation, the courses available and their fit with my mandatory bachelor courses.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Didn't get on-campus housing and first apartment (airbnb) was really bad and uncomfortable. Second apartment was really good but only minus was that it was far away from campus (10km). It was a great experience except from my housing situation.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy and accessible.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Didn't get any assistance exept from information on exchange student orientation days.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Very easy! The exchange office at UBC is great, very proactive and always physically at campus to help you immediately.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Airbnb was fine and secure but more expensive. Very hard to find good off-campus housing close to UBC...

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Its a lot more difficult to participate in spontaneous social activities with other exchange students if you have to commute 60 minutes to get there. But you will probably get a better idea of the culture and city except from the university.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Most exhange students got on-campus housing which made it har for other students to engage equally in social activities.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Worked out fine and the courses was equally available to exchange students which was a big plus.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: They needed some information + 10 courses I wanted sorted after how much i prioritized them. That was a little hard since I had to get very specific courses to get it transferred to UCPH. I didn't get the courses I wanted to in the beginning but it was easy to get them during the firts to weeks of school as people dropped the other courses.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: UBC exchange office was very kind and helpful, that really made the experience better!

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Not successful to begin with, but 2 weeks into the semester I had all the courses I wanted to. I also had to use some energy to get the courses but it turned out just fine.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Relax to begin with and wait for free spots at filled courses when the term starts.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: High level, same curriculum as UCPH, but more selfstudy and less exercise classes.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: 3rd and 4 year courses equivalent to 3rd year courses on UCPH.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: More physical learning at UCPH with valuable exercise classes, but actually pretty similar.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Econ 421 - Introductory game theory and applications
Econ 455 - International trade
Phil 369 - Philosophy of Science
Econ 333 - Economic history (...)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Phil 369 was very hard compared to UCPH but was really interesting too, and the small classes provided great circumstances for finding Canadian friends. 
Econ 333: Great teacher (Mario) and very exciting material - every class was a pleasure, and the readings was worth reading.

Food DKK per month *
Personal spending DKK per month *
Communication (phone, internet, etc.) DKK per month *
Other fees DKK per month *
What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Housing was more expensive as we got a bad house in the beginning and had to get something more expensive afterwards to get it quickly. On campus housing is very cheap though.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: A lot of clubs, very inclusive also for exchange students. Check out AMS clubs UBC to get an overview.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All of them.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join the outdoor club - it's great! Also try something new, that is really where you meet new friends.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: The mountains north of Vancouver, Whistler in the Winther, Banff (moraine lake). San Fransisco is also great (but expensive).

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, it's pretty similar to DK just a litte more open, outgoing and doesn't drink as much.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Seek clubs or courses which are not filled with exchange students. Get out of your comfort zone and take the first step, most Canadian people love to socialize;)

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Tipping culture, but its easy to get used to.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The openess to be different and the courage to be unlike everybody else. Its very multicultural, that's very cool and one of the most valuable experiences.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: See a bear, join a club doing something you are not (yet) good at, don't do it all - do all the most important things.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: There is a lot of midterm exams counting toward your final grade which can be hard if you choose tough courses but also make the final exam easier.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Making a friendgroup with Canadian students and bouldering (a lot) with one of them + my roomate.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Too establish a life away from home, friends and family, and also to get over difficulties with housing while participating in a lot of activities at the same time.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: no

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
